attributes.morphology: parallel laths and packets with width about 20 μm

evidence.quote: The microstructure of the steel tempered at 180 oC was mainly composed of tempered martensite. Some parallel martensite packets with a width of about 20 μm seemed to localize in the prior austenite grain boundaries with irregular shapes plus a preferred orientation.
There were some retained austenite grains between the martensite laths (Fig. 1a).
For the tempering temperature at 200 oC, the microstructure was still dominated by the tempered martensite.
The diffraction peak of retained austenite was in X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern embedded in Fig. 1b
The microstructure comprised both tempered martensite and tempered troostite, which implied the transformation from tempered martensite to tempered troostite (Fig. 1c).
The microstructure was tempered troostite, mainly composed of flake ferrite and flake cementite (Fig. 1d).
Fig. 3d shows the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the precipitates in Fig. 3c, which indicated that the precipitates were mainly M3C carbides.
because 23CrNi3Mo is a low carbon steel with a high Ms temperature, sufficient carbon mobility can cause cementite precipitation within the martentite [21].
